name: Deep Dim
description:
Dim Your Screens Below the Lowest Brightness Your Hardware Allows

Turned the brightness all the way down and the screen is still too bright at night? Deep Dim removes light in software, after the backlight has done all it can. A colour-matrix shader scales every pixel GNOME Shell draws, down to 1 % of the light by default, and works on any screen: laptop panels, external monitors and projectors.

Features:

* A slider in Quick Settings, right under the brightness slider, showing how much light is left
* Logarithmic slider, so every step feels like the same change
* Contrast, colour intensity and warmth controls in the slider menu
* A switch per screen, to dim one display and leave another alone
* Keyboard shortcuts with on-screen feedback: Super+Alt+Page Down / Page Up or Shift + brightness keys to step, Super+Alt+End to turn it off
* Full-screen games and videos stay dimmed
* Light dithering at strong dimming against colour banding
* No cost when off: the filter is removed completely

Deep Dim also runs on the lock screen, so locking or waking the screen at night does not flash it at full brightness, and Super+Alt+End can always undo a level that is too dark. The mouse pointer is not dimmed.

No network access, no data collected.

Bug reports and source code: https://github.com/joseteo/deepdim
